title: Fundraiser for Prairieland Political Prisoner Marciela Rueda
content:
Donate at 




https://www.gofundme.com/f/help-maricelas-family-while-she-fights-for-justice







On July 4th, during a protest at the Prairieland Detention Center in Alvarado, Tx Maricela Rueda was arrested for speaking out against the injustices of the immigrant detention system. She is currently incarcerated for taking a courageous stand in defense of dignity and justice. Maricela has always been a tireless advocate for human rights. Maricela is a mother, a daughter, a sister, and a loyal friend. Her arrest has left her family facing sudden and overwhelming challenges. Maricela’s young daughter is now without her mother’s daily love and care, and her family must also manage her estate and responsibilities while navigating the uncertainty ahead. We are asking for your support to help ease the financial strain during this heartbreaking time. All funds will go directly toward caring for her daughter and managing the urgent needs of her household. Thank you for standing in solidarity with Maricela and those who love her.

title: Illustrated Guide to Political Prisoners v19.8 released!
content:
We’ve finished the latest version of the NYC ABC “Illustrated Guide to

Political Prisoners and Prisoners of War” and it’s available for viewing

(and download) by clicking on the link below.

https://nycabc.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/nycabc_polprislisting_september-2026_legal_v02.pdf




This update includes updated mini-bios, illustrations, and address changes

for several prisoners. Unfortunately, this edition adds four of the

non-cooperating Prairieland defendants–Rowan Gibson, Autumn Hill, Mari

Rueda, and Champagne Song.

title: Bill Dunne Running Down the Walls reportback
content:
The agency of repression closed the yard for my contribution to RDTW, this weekend before the fall, 2026. The passage of time is revealing a rift between the concrete paving the small courtyards that remained open and the knees. The hamstrings and the ridiculously curved treadmills have a similar schism. So I rode an elliptical into the fray to Run Down the Walls. I let ’em have both legs three days and then again two days before the fall, 19 & 20 September. I had to do some slithering to access the venue the second day, but so it goes in life with big brother And the day before the fall, I write this report. Plus, I may have added one more means of motion to run down the walls: rowing. After my engagements on the ellipticals had ended, I wrestled the rowing machine to wring a few more gritty grains from the walls.







As my feet pushed ever forward and my arms aided and abetted, the elliptical didn’t carry me any where but figuratively. My forced presence in that physical moment, however, let me, made me, invited me me to notice the little drops of sweat hitting the concrete floor as they dripped off me. At first, just a few isolated individuals dotted the scuzzy gym floor–literal drops in the bucket, but without even a bucket.
